turns.originalText: # Core Micro Society Principles vs. Implementation Details Collective efficiency: Reducing individual time burden through shared systems Task-based organization: Work organized around specific tasks, not fixed roles or hierarchies Democratic resource planning: Community determines resource standards and priorities Capability-based authority: Implementation authority comes from demonstrated skills, not position Guaranteed basics: Core needs democratically determined and collectively guaranteed Consensus decision-making: Direct democracy for major decisions Skill-based participation: Anyone can join specialized groups through demonstrated capability Distributed expertise: Multiple approaches can coexist based on different expert perspectives Measurement-driven progress: Success defined by concrete standards and metrics Physical layout (centralized commons vs. distributed spaces) Land ownership structure (communal, private with easements, etc.) Specific guaranteed resources (what's included beyond essentials) Scale (neighborhood, village, larger community) Integration with external systems (autonomous vs. connected) Specific training methods (though AI integration is central to your concept) Housing design (though modest private/exceptional shared seems core) Formation approach (greenfield development vs. neighborhood transformation) | Approach | Medium | Medium | | Neighborhood Federation | Multiple connected areas | 7-10 years | Medium | Medium-High | Very High | | Community Land Trust | Existing or new land | 3-8 years | Medium-High |
